value.rationale: Importance-sampling robustness is a concrete design concern for residual-tracking row methods. The theorem classifies the whole natural two-probability space, isolates a sharp rare-row step-size collapse even with identical row geometry, and proves that signed mean convergence cannot diagnose mean-square stability. The exact polynomial boundary and strict optimum give decision-relevant thresholds, without claims of general-matrix applicability.
